title: An alkaline nitrite/hydrogen carrier closes an ideal cycle; process advantage is unknown
status_authority: Exact selected source bytes and scoped source reports are preserved. This incremental integration does not promote correctness, novelty, physical capability, priority, or practical advantage.
reported_status: The open-framing source gives an ideal KOH/nitrite carrier cycle and reports a nitrate/H2 cell operating point. Cross-review notes that gross HOR hydrogen is not the minimum fresh-hydrogen requirement and corrects the process accounting. The reported current density, ammonia Faradaic efficiency, and voltage do not form a single matched full-process balance.
scientific_scope_status: The source writes an ideal alkaline nitrite carrier stoichiometry. It separately reports a nitrate/H2 cell near 200 mA/cm2, 81% NH3 Faradaic efficiency, and -0.1 V; those values do not establish one complete operating-point tuple or whole-process energy. Gross hydrogen oxidation current is not fresh H2 consumption: FE_H2, recovery, purges, and other process streams must be included. Negative cell voltage alone is not net-process advantage.

proof_availability.classification_scope: The source constructions, operation calculations, and cross-review repair are preserved. No simultaneous full hydrogen balance, process energy balance, or matched system demonstration is established.
